q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 17 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 45,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per six-monthly period: 17 years = 34 periods x (Rs 45,000 / 4 = Rs 11,250) = Rs 3,82,500, under the RS (Pension) Rules.

q: Under Section 10 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, before initiating an inquiry into a complaint of sexual harassment, the Internal Complaints Committee may, at the request of the aggrieved woman, take steps to settle the matter between her and the respondent through conciliation, subject to the condition that:

options.A: The settlement so arrived at shall invariably include a monetary settlement in favour of the aggrieved woman
options.B: No monetary settlement shall be made as a basis of conciliation
options.C: The conciliation shall be conducted only by the District Officer
options.D: The respondent must first admit the allegations made against him

e: Section 10 of the POSH Act, 2013 permits conciliation at the request of the aggrieved woman before inquiry, but expressly provides that no monetary settlement shall be made as a basis of conciliation.

q: Under Section 22 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, in regard to its procedure, the Central Administrative Tribunal:

options.A: Is bound by the procedure laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 in all respects
options.B: Follows the procedure laid down in the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
options.C: Decides every case only on the basis of written documents, without hearing the parties
options.D: Is not bound by the procedure laid down in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but is guided by the principles of natural justice and has the power to regulate its own procedure

e: Section 22 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 provides that the Tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but is guided by natural justice and may regulate its own procedure.

q: Under Section 20 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, an application by or on behalf of an employee for a direction for payment of the difference between the minimum wages payable to him and the wages actually paid to him shall be presented to the Authority appointed under the Act within:

options.A: One month from the date on which the minimum wages became payable
options.B: Any time, as no period of limitation is prescribed under the Act
options.C: Three years from the date on which the minimum wages became payable
options.D: Six months from the date on which the minimum wages became payable, though the Authority may admit an application presented thereafter if the applicant had sufficient cause for not making it in time

e: Section 20 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 requires a claim application within six months of the date minimum wages became payable, though the Authority may admit a later application for sufficient cause.

q: Under Section 12 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, a contractor shall not undertake or execute any work through contract labour except:

options.A: With the verbal permission of the principal employer
options.B: After giving a notice to the trade union of the establishment
options.C: Under and in accordance with a licence issued in his favour by the licensing officer appointed under the Act
options.D: After registering himself with the Employees' State Insurance Corporation

e: Section 12 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 bars a contractor from executing work through contract labour except under and in accordance with a licence issued by the licensing officer.

q: Under Section 29 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, every rule made by the Central Government under the Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament for a total period of:

options.A: Thirty days, which may be comprised in one session or in two or more successive sessions
options.B: Seven days in one session only
options.C: Ninety days in one session only
options.D: Fifteen days, which may be comprised in two sessions

e: Section 29 of the RTI Act, 2005 requires every Central Government rule to be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days, in one session or two or more successive sessions.

q: Under Section 28 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, every registered trade union of railway servants is required to send to the Registrar of Trade Unions, annually, on or before the prescribed date:

options.A: A list of the names of all its members only
options.B: A general statement, audited in the prescribed manner, of all receipts and expenditure of the trade union during the year ending on the 31st day of December next preceding the prescribed date, together with a statement showing changes of office-bearers during the year and a copy of the rules corrected up to the date of its despatch
options.C: The minutes of every meeting held by the trade union during the year
options.D: A statement of the political fund of the trade union only

e: Section 28 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 requires every registered trade union to send the Registrar annually an audited general statement of receipts and expenditure for the year ending 31 December, with changes of office-bearers and corrected rules.

q: Under Section 23 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, no workman who is employed in any industrial establishment shall go on strike in breach of contract, and no employer of any such workman shall declare a lock-out:

options.A: On a holiday or on a weekly day of rest of the establishment
options.B: Without the prior permission of the Registrar of Trade Unions
options.C: During the pendency of conciliation proceedings before a Board and during seven days after the conclusion of such proceedings
options.D: During the period of a general election to the State Legislature

e: Section 23 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 prohibits strikes and lock-outs during the pendency of conciliation proceedings before a Board and during seven days after their conclusion.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering only 5 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 49,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Service gratuity for service under 10 years (no pension) is half a month emoluments per six-monthly period: 5 years = 10 periods x Rs 24,500 = Rs 2,45,000.

q: Under Section 18 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, where an employee is found guilty of misconduct causing financial loss to the employer, it is lawful for the employer to:

options.A: Deduct the whole of the bonus payable to the employee for the accounting year, irrespective of the amount of the loss
options.B: Recover the amount of the loss from the Provident Fund balance of the employee
options.C: Withhold the bonus of all the employees of the establishment for that accounting year
options.D: Deduct the amount of the loss so caused from the amount of bonus payable by him to the employee under the Act in respect of the accounting year in which the employee is found guilty of the misconduct

e: Section 18 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 permits deduction of the financial loss caused by misconduct from the bonus payable to that employee for the accounting year in which he is found guilty.

q: Under Section 5 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the appropriate Government may, by notification and subject to such conditions as may be specified therein, exempt any establishment or class of employees from the operation of the provisions of the Act if, in its opinion:

options.A: The establishment has not completed five years of its existence
options.B: The employees of the establishment are already in receipt of gratuity or pensionary benefits not less favourable than the benefits conferred under the Act
options.C: The employer has applied for exemption on the ground of financial hardship alone
options.D: The employees of the establishment have passed a resolution seeking such exemption

e: Section 5 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 permits exemption by notification only where employees are already in receipt of gratuity or pensionary benefits not less favourable than those under the Act.

q: Under Section 20 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, the Commissioners for employees' compensation, for the areas specified by it, are appointed by:

options.A: The Central Government, in every case
options.B: The employer of the establishment concerned
options.C: The State Government, by notification in the Official Gazette
options.D: The High Court of the State

e: Section 20 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 provides that Commissioners for employees compensation are appointed by the State Government by notification in the Official Gazette.

q: Under Section 14 of the Apprentices Act, 1961, where Act Apprentices are undergoing training in a factory, such as a railway workshop, the provisions of the Factories Act, 1948 relating to the health, safety and welfare of workers:

options.A: Do not apply to the apprentices in any case, as an apprentice is a trainee and not a worker
options.B: Apply only to apprentices who have completed one year of training
options.C: Apply only if the employer voluntarily opts for their application
options.D: Apply in relation to the health, safety and welfare of the apprentices as if they were workers within the meaning of that Act

e: Section 14 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 applies the Factories Act, 1948 provisions on health, safety and welfare to apprentices in a factory as if they were workers under that Act.

q: Under Section 13 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, on the completion of an inquiry into a complaint of sexual harassment, the Internal Complaints Committee shall provide a report of its findings to the employer within:

options.A: Ten days of the completion of the inquiry
options.B: Thirty days of the completion of the inquiry
options.C: Sixty days of the completion of the inquiry
options.D: Ninety days of the completion of the inquiry

e: Section 13 of the POSH Act, 2013 requires the Internal Complaints Committee to provide its report of findings to the employer within ten days of completion of the inquiry.

q: Under Section 33 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, the provisions of the Act:

options.A: Are subject to the provisions of every other law for the time being in force
options.B: Have effect only where they are consistent with the Railway Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules
options.C: Shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force or in any instrument having effect by virtue of any law other than the Act
options.D: Have ceased to have effect after the constitution of the State Administrative Tribunals

e: Section 33 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 gives the Act overriding effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any other law or in any instrument having effect by virtue of any such law.

q: Under Section 6 of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946, an employer, workman, trade union or other prescribed representative of workmen, aggrieved by the order of the Certifying Officer certifying the standing orders of an industrial establishment, may appeal to the appellate authority within:

options.A: Fifteen days from the date on which the copies of the order are sent by the Certifying Officer
options.B: Sixty days from the date on which the copies of the order are sent by the Certifying Officer
options.C: Ninety days from the date on which the copies of the order are sent by the Certifying Officer
options.D: Thirty days from the date on which the copies of the order are sent by the Certifying Officer

e: Section 6 of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 permits an appeal against certification of standing orders within thirty days from the date copies of the order are sent by the Certifying Officer.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 67,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the enhanced rate, at 50 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:
e: Family pension at the enhanced rate is 50 percent of last basic pay under the RS (Pension) Rules: 50 percent x Rs 67,000 = Rs 33,500.

q: Under Section 30 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, if any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of the Act, the Central Government may, by order published in the Official Gazette, make such provisions, not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act, as appear to it to be necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty, provided that no such order shall be made after the expiry of:

options.A: One year from the commencement of the Act
options.B: Five years from the commencement of the Act
options.C: Two years from the commencement of the Act
options.D: Ten years from the commencement of the Act

e: Section 30 of the RTI Act, 2005 bars any difficulty-removal order after the expiry of two years from the commencement of the Act.

q: Under Section 29 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a person who commits a breach of any term of a settlement or award which is binding on him under the Act is punishable with:

options.A: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine, or with both, and with an additional fine for every day during which the breach continues after conviction
options.B: Fine only, not exceeding one hundred rupees in all
options.C: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years in every case
options.D: No punishment, as a breach of a settlement or award has only civil consequences

e: Section 29 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 punishes breach of a binding settlement or award with imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both, plus an additional fine for each day the breach continues after conviction.

q: Under Section 22 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, a dispute between an employer and his employees with respect to the bonus payable under the Act, or with respect to the application of the Act to an establishment in the public sector, shall be:

options.A: Decided finally by the employer himself
options.B: Decided by the Registrar of Trade Unions
options.C: Referred to the controlling authority under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972
options.D: Deemed to be an industrial dispute within the meaning of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947

e: Section 22 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 deems a dispute on bonus payable, or on application of the Act to a public sector establishment, to be an industrial dispute under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

q: Under Section 7(7) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, a person aggrieved by an order of the controlling authority determining the amount of gratuity payable may prefer an appeal to the appropriate Government or such other authority as may be specified by it within:

options.A: Thirty days from the date of the receipt of the order
options.B: Ninety days from the date of the receipt of the order
options.C: Sixty days from the date of the receipt of the order, though the appellate authority may admit an appeal presented thereafter, within a further period not exceeding sixty days, if it is satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from preferring it in time
options.D: One year from the date of the receipt of the order

e: Section 7(7) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 allows an appeal against the controlling authority within sixty days of receipt of the order, extendable by a further period not exceeding sixty days for sufficient cause.

q: Under Section 28 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where an agreement for the commutation of half-monthly payments, or an agreement in regard to the amount of compensation payable to an employee, has been arrived at, a memorandum of the agreement shall be sent by the employer to the Commissioner, who shall:

options.A: Return the memorandum to the employer without recording it
options.B: Forward the memorandum to the State Government for approval
options.C: Refer the memorandum to the Labour Court for adjudication
options.D: Record the memorandum in a register in the prescribed manner, after he is satisfied as to its genuineness

e: Section 28 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 requires the Commissioner to record a memorandum of agreement in the prescribed register after he is satisfied as to its genuineness.

q: Under Section 10 of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946, the standing orders finally certified under the Act shall not, except on an agreement between the employer and the workmen, be liable to modification until the expiry of:

options.A: Six months from the date on which they or the last modifications thereof came into operation
options.B: One month from the date on which they came into operation
options.C: Two years from the date on which they came into operation
options.D: Five years from the date on which they came into operation

e: Section 10 of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 bars modification of finally certified standing orders, except by agreement, until six months from the date they or the last modification came into operation.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 220 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 55,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent of the basic pay. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him will be:
e: Leave encashment is (pay + DA) x days / 30: (Rs 55,000 + Rs 27,500) = Rs 82,500; Rs 82,500 / 30 x 220 days = Rs 6,05,000.

q: Under Section 41H of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, where the workers employed in a factory consider that there is a likelihood of imminent danger to their lives or health due to any accident, they may bring the same to the notice of the occupier, agent, manager or other person in charge of the factory, and to the Inspector of Factories, whereupon:

options.A: The workers are liable to be punished for raising a false alarm
options.B: The matter shall be decided finally by the trade union of the workers
options.C: The factory shall be closed permanently by the Inspector in every such case
options.D: The occupier shall take immediate remedial action if he is satisfied about the existence of such danger and send a report forthwith to the Inspector; if he is not so satisfied, he shall nevertheless refer the matter forthwith to the Inspector, whose decision on the question shall be final

e: Section 41H of the Factories Act, 1948 requires the occupier to take immediate remedial action on a report of imminent danger and inform the Inspector forthwith, or refer the matter to the Inspector forthwith if not satisfied, the Inspector decision being final.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 6 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 61,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at twelve times the emoluments as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: Death gratuity for 5 to 11 years of service is 12x emoluments under the RS (Pension) Rules: 12 x Rs 61,000 = Rs 7,32,000.

q: Under Section 4 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, Conciliation Officers, who are charged with the duty of mediating in and promoting the settlement of industrial disputes, are appointed by:

options.A: The appropriate Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, in such number as it thinks fit
options.B: The Chief Labour Commissioner, by an order issued in his own name
options.C: The Labour Court having jurisdiction over the establishment
options.D: The Registrar of Trade Unions of the State concerned

e: Section 4 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 provides that Conciliation Officers are appointed by the appropriate Government by notification in the Official Gazette, in such number as it thinks fit.

q: Under Section 20 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, the Act applies to an establishment in the public sector only if the establishment sells the goods produced by it, or renders services, in competition with an establishment in the private sector, and the income from such sale or services, or both, is not less than the following proportion of its gross income:

options.A: Ten per cent
options.B: Fifty per cent
options.C: Twenty per cent
options.D: Thirty-three and one-third per cent

e: Section 20 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 applies the Act to a public sector establishment only if its income from competitive sale or services is not less than twenty percent of its gross income.

q: Under Section 7(4) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, where there is a dispute as to the amount of gratuity admissible to an employee, or as to the admissibility of a claim or the person entitled to receive the gratuity, the dispute shall be decided by:

options.A: The employer himself, whose decision shall be final
options.B: The Labour Court of the district in the first instance
options.C: The Registrar of Trade Unions
options.D: The controlling authority appointed under the Act, after giving the parties a reasonable opportunity of being heard

e: Section 7(4) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 requires a dispute on the amount, admissibility or person entitled to gratuity to be decided by the controlling authority after giving the parties a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

q: Under Section 19 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where a question arises in any proceeding under the Act as to the liability of any person to pay compensation, or as to the amount or duration of compensation, and the question cannot be settled by the agreement of the parties, it shall be settled by:

options.A: The employer, subject to the approval of the Inspector
options.B: The District Magistrate of the area
options.C: The High Court, in the exercise of its original jurisdiction
options.D: A Commissioner appointed under the Act

e: Section 19 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 provides that questions on liability, amount or duration of compensation that cannot be settled by agreement shall be settled by a Commissioner.

q: Under Section 6 of the Apprentices Act, 1961, in regard to the period of apprenticeship training of an Act Apprentice engaged in a railway workshop, the correct position is that:

options.A: The period of training shall be the period specified in the contract of apprenticeship, and the training shall be deemed to have commenced on the date on which the contract of apprenticeship comes into force
options.B: The period of training is uniformly three years for apprentices of every designated trade
options.C: The period of training commences only on the date on which the apprentice attains the age of eighteen years
options.D: The period of training may be curtailed or extended by the employer at his discretion, without reference to the contract

e: Section 6 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 provides that the training period is the period specified in the apprenticeship contract and training is deemed to commence on the date the contract comes into force.

q: Under Section 15 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, for the purpose of determining the sums to be paid to the aggrieved woman by way of compensation, the Internal Complaints Committee shall have regard to, among other things:

options.A: Only the basic pay last drawn by the respondent
options.B: Only the length of service of the respondent in the establishment
options.C: The mental trauma, pain, suffering and emotional distress caused to the aggrieved woman, the loss in her career opportunity, the medical expenses incurred by her, and the income and financial status of the respondent
options.D: The profits earned by the establishment in the accounting year in which the complaint was made

e: Section 15 of the POSH Act, 2013 requires compensation to be determined with regard to the mental trauma, pain, suffering and emotional distress caused, loss of career opportunity, medical expenses, and the income and financial status of the respondent.

q: Under Section 20 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, an application by a railway servant shall not ordinarily be admitted by the Central Administrative Tribunal unless:

options.A: The applicant has first obtained the written permission of his controlling officer
options.B: The applicant had availed of all the remedies available to him under the relevant service rules as to redressal of his grievances, and the Tribunal is satisfied in that regard
options.C: The applicant has deposited security for the costs of the opposite party
options.D: A period of five years has elapsed from the date of the order complained against

e: Section 20 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 bars admission of an application unless the applicant has availed of all remedies available under the relevant service rules for redressal of grievances.

q: Under Section 13 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, in respect of an employee in a scheduled employment, such as that of contract labour engaged on railway works, the appropriate Government may:

options.A: Fix the rates of overtime wages only, leaving the hours of work to the employer
options.B: Fix the number of hours of work which shall constitute a normal working day, inclusive of intervals for rest, and provide for a day of rest in every period of seven days
options.C: Direct that no register of wages shall be maintained by the employer
options.D: Exempt the employer from the payment of wages in cash in every case

e: Section 13 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 empowers the appropriate Government to fix the hours constituting a normal working day, inclusive of rest intervals, and provide a day of rest in every seven days.

q: Under Section 10 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, the employment of contract labour in any process, operation or other work in an establishment, such as a railway establishment, may be prohibited by:

options.A: The appropriate Government, by notification in the Official Gazette, after consultation with the Central Advisory Board or the State Advisory Board, as the case may be
options.B: The principal employer, by an order displayed on the notice board of the establishment
options.C: The contractor, by a notice served on the principal employer
options.D: The Inspector appointed under the Act, by an order in writing served on the contractor

e: Section 10 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 empowers only the appropriate Government, by Gazette notification after consulting the Central or State Advisory Board, to prohibit contract labour in a process or work.

q: Under Section 7 of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946, the standing orders finally certified under the Act shall, unless an appeal has been preferred against their certification, come into operation on the expiry of the following period from the date on which the authenticated copies thereof are sent by the Certifying Officer to the employer and the workmen:

options.A: Seven days
options.B: Ninety days
options.C: Thirty days
options.D: Six months

e: Section 7 of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 provides that finally certified standing orders come into operation on expiry of thirty days from the date authenticated copies are sent, unless an appeal is preferred.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 14 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 63,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per six-monthly period: 14 years = 28 periods x (Rs 63,000 / 4 = Rs 15,750) = Rs 4,41,000.

q: Under Section 5 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a Board of Conciliation constituted by the appropriate Government for promoting the settlement of an industrial dispute shall consist of:

options.A: A Chairman only, with no other member
options.B: A Chairman and two or four other members, the Chairman being an independent person and the other members representing the parties to the dispute in equal numbers
options.C: Five members, all of whom shall be officers of the appropriate Government
options.D: Two members, both of whom shall be nominees of the employer

e: Section 5 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 provides that a Board of Conciliation consists of a Chairman, an independent person, and two or four other members representing the parties in equal numbers.

q: Under Section 23 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, where an employee or a trade union of employees seeks any information from an employer in a dispute regarding bonus, the correct position in regard to the audited balance sheet and profit and loss account of the employer, being a company, is that:

options.A: The balance sheet and the profit and loss account shall be treated as wholly inadmissible in evidence
options.B: The employer must prove the accuracy of every entry therein by oral evidence in every case
options.C: No presumption of accuracy attaches to an audited balance sheet under any circumstance
options.D: The audited balance sheet and profit and loss account shall be presumed to be accurate, and it shall not be necessary for the employer to prove their accuracy

e: Section 23 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 provides that the audited balance sheet and profit and loss account of a company employer shall be presumed accurate and need not be proved by the employer.

q: Under Section 7(5) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, for the purpose of conducting an inquiry into a dispute regarding gratuity, the controlling authority shall have:

options.A: The same powers as are vested in a court, while trying a suit, under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in respect of enforcing the attendance of any person, examining him on oath and compelling the production of documents
options.B: The power to impose any penalty prescribed under the Indian Penal Code
options.C: No power to summon any witness or to call for any document
options.D: The power to decide the dispute only on the basis of the written statement of the employer

e: Section 7(5) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 gives the controlling authority, for inquiry, the powers of a court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 for enforcing attendance, examining on oath and compelling production of documents.

q: Under Section 25 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, in regard to the method of recording evidence in a proceeding before a Commissioner under the Act, the correct position is that:

options.A: The evidence of every witness must be recorded verbatim by a stenographer in every case
options.B: No record of the evidence of any witness shall be made at all
options.C: The Commissioner shall make a brief memorandum of the substance of the evidence of each witness, as the examination of the witness proceeds
options.D: The evidence shall be recorded only by the legal practitioners of the parties

e: Section 25 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 requires the Commissioner to make a brief memorandum of the substance of the evidence of each witness as the examination proceeds.

q: Under Section 8 of the Apprentices Act, 1961, the number of apprentices, or the ratio of apprentices to workers, to be engaged in a designated trade in an establishment, such as a railway workshop, is determined by:

options.A: The Central Government, after consulting the Central Apprenticeship Council, by notification in the Official Gazette
options.B: The employer of the establishment, at his sole discretion
options.C: The trade union functioning in the establishment
options.D: The Inspector of Factories of the area

e: Section 8 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 provides that the number of apprentices or the ratio for a designated trade is determined by the Central Government after consulting the Central Apprenticeship Council, by Gazette notification.

q: Under Section 17 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, a person who contravenes the prohibition, contained in Section 16 of the Act, on publishing or making known the contents of a complaint of sexual harassment and of the inquiry proceedings relating thereto, shall be liable to a penalty of:

options.A: Rs 500

e: Section 17 of the POSH Act, 2013 prescribes a penalty of Rs 5,000 for contravening the Section 16 prohibition on publishing or making known the contents of a complaint and inquiry proceedings.

q: Under Section 14 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, the Central Administrative Tribunal exercises jurisdiction, powers and authority in relation to:

options.A: Only the fixation of pay of railway servants on promotion
options.B: Recruitment, and matters concerning recruitment, to services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union, and all service matters concerning the persons appointed to such services and posts
options.C: Only the conduct of departmental examinations on the Railways
options.D: Only disputes between two railway servants in their private capacity

e: Section 14 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 gives the Central Administrative Tribunal jurisdiction over recruitment and all service matters concerning persons appointed to services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union.

q: Under Section 14 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, where an employee in a scheduled employment works on any day in excess of the number of hours constituting a normal working day, he shall be entitled to wages for the overtime work at:

options.A: The ordinary rate of wages admissible to him for a normal working day
options.B: Half of the ordinary rate of wages admissible to him
options.C: The overtime rate fixed under the Minimum Wages Act, or the overtime rate fixed under any other law of the appropriate Government in force, whichever is higher
options.D: A rate to be settled by the employer in each individual case

e: Section 14 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 entitles an employee working beyond a normal working day to overtime wages at the overtime rate under that Act or under any other law of the appropriate Government, whichever is higher.

q: Under Section 16 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, where contract labour numbering one hundred or more is ordinarily employed by a contractor in an establishment, one or more canteens for the use of such contract labour shall be provided and maintained by:

options.A: The appropriate Government
options.B: The contractor
options.C: The trade union of the contract labour
options.D: The Inspector appointed under the Act

e: Section 16 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 requires the contractor to provide and maintain canteens where one hundred or more contract labour are ordinarily employed by him.

q: Under Section 4 of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946, standing orders submitted by an employer shall be certifiable under the Act if provision is made therein for every matter set out in the Schedule to the Act applicable to the establishment and the standing orders are otherwise in conformity with the Act, and it shall be the function of the Certifying Officer or the appellate authority, as the case may be, to adjudicate upon:

options.A: The quantum of bonus payable to the workmen of the establishment
options.B: The seniority of the workmen inter se
options.C: The wages payable for overtime work in the establishment
options.D: The fairness or reasonableness of the provisions contained in the standing orders

e: Section 4 of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 makes standing orders certifiable if they cover every applicable Schedule matter and conform to the Act, and makes it the function of the Certifying Officer or appellate authority to adjudicate on their fairness or reasonableness.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering only 4 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 69,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Service gratuity for service under 10 years is half a month emoluments per six-monthly period: 4 years = 8 periods x Rs 34,500 = Rs 2,76,000.

q: Under Section 7B of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, constitute one or more National Industrial Tribunals for the adjudication of industrial disputes which, in its opinion:

options.A: Involve questions of national importance, or are of such a nature that industrial establishments situated in more than one State are likely to be interested in, or affected by, such disputes
options.B: Relate to a single workman employed in a single establishment
options.C: Arise exclusively out of the fixation of the wages of one employee
options.D: Have already been decided by a Labour Court and are pending in appeal

e: Section 7B of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 empowers the Central Government to constitute National Industrial Tribunals for disputes involving questions of national importance or affecting establishments in more than one State.

q: Under Section 31A of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, where the employees of an establishment have entered into an agreement or settlement with the employer for the payment of an annual bonus linked with production or productivity in lieu of bonus based on allocable surplus, the employees shall be entitled to receive bonus under such agreement or settlement, subject to the condition that it shall not exceed:

options.A: Eight and one-third per cent of the salary or wage earned by them during the accounting year
options.B: Sixteen and two-third per cent of such salary or wage
options.C: Twenty per cent of the salary or wage earned by them during the accounting year
options.D: Fifty per cent of the salary or wage earned by them during the accounting year

e: Section 31A of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 caps bonus under a production or productivity linked agreement or settlement in lieu of surplus-based bonus at twenty percent of the salary or wage earned in the accounting year.

q: Under Section 9(2) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, an employer who contravenes any of the provisions of the Act, or makes a default in complying with any of them, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which:

options.A: Shall be only up to one month in every case
options.B: May extend to six months at the most
options.C: Shall be up to three months, or with fine only
options.D: Shall not be less than three months but may extend to one year, or with fine which shall not be less than ten thousand rupees but may extend to twenty thousand rupees, or with both

e: Section 9(2) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 punishes contravention of the Act with imprisonment of not less than three months and up to one year, or fine of not less than Rs 10,000 and up to Rs 20,000, or both.

q: Under Section 27 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where a question of law arises in a proceeding before a Commissioner under the Act, the Commissioner may:

options.A: Decide the question himself finally, with no reference to any court
options.B: Submit the question for the decision of the High Court, and shall decide the proceeding in conformity with such decision
options.C: Refer the question to the employer for his opinion
options.D: Refer the question to the District Magistrate for his decision

e: Section 27 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 permits a Commissioner to submit a question of law for the decision of the High Court and to decide the proceeding in conformity with that decision.

q: Under Section 37 of the Apprentices Act, 1961, the power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act vests in:

options.A: The employer of each establishment engaging apprentices
options.B: The State Government of the State in which the establishment is situated, in every case
options.C: The Central Government, which may, after consulting the Central Apprenticeship Council, by notification in the Official Gazette, make such rules
options.D: The Registrar of Trade Unions

e: Section 37 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 vests rule-making power in the Central Government, exercisable after consulting the Central Apprenticeship Council, by notification in the Official Gazette.

q: Under Section 21 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, the Internal Complaints Committee of a workplace is required to prepare, in each calendar year, an annual report and forward the same to:

options.A: The employer and the District Officer
options.B: The Registrar of Trade Unions only
options.C: The Labour Court only
options.D: No authority, as the report is meant only for the internal record of the Committee

e: Section 21 of the POSH Act, 2013 requires the Internal Complaints Committee to prepare an annual report in each calendar year and forward it to the employer and the District Officer.

q: Under Section 28 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, in respect of any matter in relation to which the Central Administrative Tribunal has jurisdiction under the Act, no court shall have, or be entitled to exercise, any jurisdiction, powers or authority, except:

options.A: The court of the District Judge of the district concerned
options.B: The Supreme Court, or a High Court exercising jurisdiction under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution
options.C: The Labour Court constituted under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
options.D: The Railway Rates Tribunal

e: Section 28 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 excludes the jurisdiction of all courts in matters within the Tribunal jurisdiction, except the Supreme Court and a High Court under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution.

q: Under Section 18 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, every employer of employees in a scheduled employment is required to:

options.A: Display the balance sheet of his establishment at the main entrance
options.B: Obtain the prior approval of the Inspector for every wage period
options.C: Pay the wages of his employees only through a trade union
options.D: Maintain such registers and records, giving such particulars of the employees employed by him, the nature of work performed by them and the wages paid to them, as may be prescribed, and keep them available for inspection

e: Section 18 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 requires every employer to maintain prescribed registers and records of employees, work performed and wages paid, and keep them available for inspection.

q: Under Section 20 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, if any amenity required to be provided under the Act for the benefit of the contract labour, such as rest rooms, drinking water, first-aid facilities or a canteen, is not provided by the contractor within the prescribed time, such amenity shall be provided by:

options.A: The appropriate Government, at its own cost in every case
options.B: The trade union of the contract labour, at its own cost
options.C: The principal employer, within such time as may be prescribed, and the expenses incurred by him in providing the amenity may be recovered by him from the contractor
options.D: No person, and the contract labour shall remain without the amenity

e: Section 20 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 requires the principal employer to provide any prescribed amenity not provided by the contractor in time, recovering the expenses from the contractor.

q: Under Section 13A of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946, if any question arises as to the application or interpretation of a standing order certified under the Act, the question may be referred by the employer, or by any workman, trade union or other prescribed representative of workmen, for decision to:

options.A: The Registrar of Trade Unions
options.B: The District Magistrate of the area
options.C: The Inspector of Factories of the area
options.D: Any one of the Labour Courts specified for the purpose by the appropriate Government, whose decision thereon shall be final and binding on all the parties

e: Section 13A of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 allows a question on application or interpretation of a certified standing order to be referred to a specified Labour Court, whose decision is final and binding.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 28 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 58,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Death gratuity for 20 years or more is half a month emoluments per six-monthly period, capped at 33x: 28 years = 56 periods x Rs 29,000 = Rs 16,24,000, below the cap of Rs 19,14,000.

q: Under Section 12 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, where a settlement is arrived at in the course of conciliation proceedings in an industrial dispute, the Conciliation Officer shall:

options.A: Send a report thereof to the appropriate Government, together with a memorandum of the settlement signed by the parties to the dispute
options.B: Keep the settlement only in his personal file, without informing the Government
options.C: Refer the settlement to the Labour Court for its approval in every case
options.D: Announce the settlement in a newspaper circulating in the area

e: Section 12 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 requires the Conciliation Officer, on a settlement in conciliation, to send a report to the appropriate Government with a memorandum of settlement signed by the parties.

q: Under Section 34 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, subject to the provisions of Section 31A of the Act, the provisions of the Act shall:

options.A: Have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law for the time being in force, or in the terms of any award, agreement, settlement or contract of service
options.B: Apply only where they are more favourable to the employer than the terms of a settlement
options.C: Have no effect where a contract of service contains a different term
options.D: Apply only to establishments in the private sector

e: Section 34 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, subject to Section 31A, gives the Act overriding effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any other law or in any award, agreement, settlement or contract of service.

q: Under Section 29 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, where a memorandum of an agreement for the payment of compensation ought to have been registered under the Act, but has not been so registered, the position is that:

options.A: The employee forfeits the whole of the compensation payable to him
options.B: The employer is absolved of all liability to pay compensation
options.C: The employer shall be liable to pay the full amount of compensation payable by him under the Act in respect of the injury, and, notwithstanding any contract to the contrary, no half-monthly payment paid to the employee shall be deducted therefrom
options.D: The agreement becomes binding on the Commissioner without registration in every case

e: Section 29 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 makes the employer liable for the full compensation where a required memorandum of agreement is not registered, with no deduction of half-monthly payments already paid, despite any contract to the contrary.

q: Under Section 26 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, an employer who fails to comply with the provisions of the Act, including the obligation to constitute an Internal Complaints Committee, shall be punishable with a fine which may extend to:

options.C: Rs 500

e: Section 26 of the POSH Act, 2013 punishes an employer failing to comply with the Act, including failure to constitute an Internal Complaints Committee, with a fine which may extend to Rs 50,000.

q: Under Section 27 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, the appropriate Government may add any employment to Part I or Part II of the Schedule to the Act, in respect of which it is of opinion that minimum rates of wages should be fixed, after:

options.A: Obtaining the orders of the High Court in every case
options.B: Consulting the employer concerned alone
options.C: Giving not less than one month's notice of its intention by notification
options.D: Giving by notification in the Official Gazette not less than two months' notice of its intention so to do

e: Section 27 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 permits addition of an employment to the Schedule only after giving, by Gazette notification, not less than two months notice of the intention to do so.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 91,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the normal rate, at 30 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 45,500 per month
options.B: Rs 18,200 per month
options.C: Rs 27,300 per month
options.D: Rs 36,400 per month

e: Family pension at the normal rate is 30 percent of last basic pay under the RS (Pension) Rules: 30 percent x Rs 91,000 = Rs 27,300 per month.

q: Under Section 21 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, in regard to matters which are required to be kept confidential, the correct position is that there shall not be included in any report or award published under the Act any information obtained by a Conciliation Officer, Board, Court or arbitrator in the course of an investigation or inquiry as to a trade union or as to an individual business, not intended for public knowledge, except:

options.A: Where the employer alone consents to the disclosure
options.B: In so far as the trade union or the person carrying on the business, as the case may be, has given written consent to such disclosure
options.C: Where a period of ten years has elapsed since the information was obtained
options.D: Where the Conciliation Officer considers the disclosure to be in public interest

e: Section 21 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 bars inclusion of confidential information on a trade union or individual business in a published report or award, except in so far as the trade union or the person concerned has given written consent.

q: Under Section 36 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, if the appropriate Government, having regard to the financial position and other relevant circumstances of any establishment or class of establishments, is of the opinion that it will not be in public interest to apply all or any of the provisions of the Act thereto, it may:

options.A: By notification in the Official Gazette, exempt such establishment or class of establishments from all or any of the provisions of the Act for such period as may be specified in the notification, and subject to such conditions, if any, as it may think fit to impose
options.B: Direct the employees of the establishment to forego bonus permanently in every case
options.C: Transfer the establishment to the private sector
options.D: Exempt the establishment only by an order of the High Court

e: Section 36 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 empowers the appropriate Government, in public interest and having regard to financial position and other circumstances, to exempt an establishment by Gazette notification for a specified period and on specified conditions.

q: Under Section 14 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, where the Internal Complaints Committee arrives at a conclusion that the allegation of sexual harassment against the respondent is malicious, or that the complaint has been made knowing it to be false, it may recommend action against the complainant in accordance with the service rules applicable to her; but in this regard, the correct position is that:

options.A: Every complaint which is not fully proved must necessarily be treated as a false complaint
options.B: The complainant is liable to be dismissed from service in every such case
options.C: The Committee has no power to recommend any action even where the complaint is proved to be malicious
options.D: Mere inability to substantiate the complaint, or to provide adequate proof in support of it, need not attract action against the complainant

e: Section 14 of the POSH Act, 2013 permits action only for a malicious or knowingly false complaint; mere inability to substantiate the complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant.

q: Under Section 34 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, in regard to the cognizance of offences punishable under the Act, the correct position is that:

options.A: Any police officer may take cognizance of such an offence on his own information
options.B: Any workman of the establishment may prosecute the employer without any sanction
options.C: No court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under the Act, or of the abetment of any such offence, except on a complaint made by, or under the authority of, the appropriate Government
options.D: Only the Labour Court may take cognizance of such an offence, on a reference made by the employer

e: Section 34 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 provides that no court shall take cognizance of an offence under the Act, or its abetment, except on a complaint made by or under the authority of the appropriate Government.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation with 170 days of Leave on Average Pay at his credit. His basic pay at retirement is Rs 51,000 per month and Dearness Allowance is admissible at 50 per cent of the basic pay. The cash equivalent of leave salary payable to him, worked out at the rate of pay plus dearness allowance for each day of leave divided by 30, will be:
e: Leave encashment is (pay + DA) / 30 x days: (Rs 51,000 + Rs 25,500) / 30 x 170 = Rs 2,550 x 170 = Rs 4,33,500.

q: Under Section 10 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, Certifying Surgeons, whose duties include the examination and certification of young persons employed in a factory and the examination of persons engaged in dangerous occupations or processes, are appointed by:

options.A: The occupier of the factory
options.B: The State Government, which may appoint qualified medical practitioners to be certifying surgeons for such purposes and assign them local limits
options.C: The manager of the factory
options.D: The Inspector of Factories of the area

e: Section 10 of the Factories Act, 1948 provides that Certifying Surgeons are appointed by the State Government from qualified medical practitioners, with assigned local limits, for examination and certification duties.

q: Under Section 6 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a Court of Inquiry, which may be constituted by the appropriate Government for inquiring into any matter appearing to be connected with, or relevant to, an industrial dispute, shall consist of:

options.A: The presiding officer of a Labour Court alone
options.B: Two representatives each of the employer and the workmen
options.C: One or more independent persons, as the appropriate Government may think fit
options.D: The Conciliation Officer having jurisdiction over the area

e: Section 6 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 provides that a Court of Inquiry consists of one or more independent persons, as the appropriate Government may think fit.

q: Under Section 13 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, where an employee has not worked for all the working days in an accounting year, the bonus payable to him under the Act for that accounting year shall:

options.A: The minimum bonus of one hundred rupees, or sixty rupees as the case may be, if such bonus is higher than 8.33 per cent of his salary or wage for the days he has worked in that accounting year, shall be proportionately reduced
options.B: Be paid in full irrespective of the number of days worked
options.C: Be forfeited in full for that accounting year
options.D: Be deferred and paid along with the bonus of the next accounting year

e: Section 13 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 provides for proportionate reduction where the employee has not worked all working days, the statutory minimum bonus of Rs 100 or Rs 60 applying if it exceeds 8.33 percent for the days worked.

q: Under Section 14 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the correct position in regard to the effect of the provisions of the Act is that:

options.A: The provisions of the Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other enactment, or in any instrument or contract having effect by virtue of any such enactment
options.B: The provisions of the Act shall apply only where they are more favourable than the terms of a contract of service
options.C: The provisions of the Act shall have no effect where an award or settlement provides otherwise
options.D: The provisions of the Act shall apply only to establishments in the private sector

e: Section 14 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 gives the Act overriding effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any other enactment or in any instrument or contract having effect under such enactment.

q: Under Section 21 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, the proceedings in respect of a claim for compensation under the Act shall ordinarily be held before the Commissioner for the area in which:

options.A: The head office of the employer is situated in every case
options.B: The accident took place resulting in the injury, or the employee claiming compensation ordinarily resides, or the employer has his registered office
options.C: The employee was recruited into service
options.D: The trade union of the employee has its registered office

e: Section 21 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 fixes venue ordinarily before the Commissioner for the area where the accident took place, or where the claimant ordinarily resides, or where the employer has his registered office.

q: Under Section 16 of the Apprentices Act, 1961, if personal injury is caused to an Act Apprentice in a railway workshop by an accident arising out of, and in the course of, his apprenticeship training, the compensation payable to him shall be paid:

options.A: At a flat rate fixed by the employer in each case
options.B: Only if the apprentice has completed one year of training
options.C: By the State Government out of its own funds in every case
options.D: By his employer, in accordance with the provisions of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923, as modified by the Schedule to the Apprentices Act

e: Section 16 of the Apprentices Act, 1961 makes compensation for personal injury to an apprentice from an accident arising out of and in the course of training payable by the employer under the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 as modified by the Schedule to the Apprentices Act.

q: A railway servant dies while in service after completing 13 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of his death are Rs 57,000 per month. The death gratuity payable to his family, at twenty times the emoluments as admissible for this length of service, will be:
e: Death gratuity for 11 to 20 years of service is 20x emoluments under the RS (Pension) Rules: 20 x Rs 57,000 = Rs 11,40,000.

q: Under Section 88A of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, in regard to the notice of certain dangerous occurrences in a factory, the correct position is that:

options.A: Notice is required to be sent only where the dangerous occurrence results in the death of a worker in the factory
options.B: The manager of the factory shall send a notice thereof, in the prescribed form and within the prescribed time, to the prescribed authorities, where a dangerous occurrence of the prescribed nature takes place in the factory, whether it causes any bodily injury or disability or not
options.C: Notice is required to be sent only where the bodily injury caused by the occurrence prevents the injured worker from working for a period of forty-eight hours or more
options.D: No notice is required to be sent where the dangerous occurrence does not result in any bodily injury to a worker

e: Section 88A of the Factories Act, 1948 requires the manager to send notice of a prescribed dangerous occurrence to the prescribed authorities whether or not it causes bodily injury or disability.

q: Under Section 16 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, in regard to the form of a report or an award under the Act, the correct position is that:

options.A: The award of a Labour Court, Tribunal or National Tribunal shall be in writing and shall be signed by its presiding officer
options.B: The award of a Labour Court may be pronounced orally and need not be signed
options.C: The report of a Board or Court need not be signed by any member
options.D: The award shall be signed by the representatives of both the parties to the dispute

e: Section 16 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 requires the award of a Labour Court, Tribunal or National Tribunal to be in writing and signed by its presiding officer.

q: Under Section 15 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, where, in any accounting year, the allocable surplus exceeds the amount of maximum bonus payable to the employees, the excess, subject to a limit of twenty per cent of the total salary or wage of the employees employed in the establishment in that accounting year, shall be:

options.A: Paid to the employees as additional bonus in the same accounting year
options.B: Credited to the general revenues of the appropriate Government
options.C: Carried forward for being set on in the succeeding accounting years, up to and inclusive of the fourth accounting year, in the prescribed manner
options.D: Transferred to the reserve fund of the establishment permanently

e: Section 15 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 requires excess allocable surplus, subject to a limit of twenty percent of total salary or wage, to be carried forward for set-on in succeeding accounting years up to and including the fourth year.

q: Under Section 2(s) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, 'wages', as defined in the Act, means all emoluments earned by an employee while on duty or on leave, in accordance with the terms and conditions of his employment, which are paid or are payable to him in cash, and:

options.A: Includes bonus, commission, house rent allowance and overtime wages
options.B: Includes dearness allowance, but does not include any bonus, commission, house rent allowance, overtime wages or any other allowance
options.C: Excludes dearness allowance in every case
options.D: Includes every allowance drawn by the employee without exception

e: Section 2(s) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 defines wages to include dearness allowance but to exclude bonus, commission, house rent allowance, overtime wages and any other allowance.

q: Under Section 5 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, the District Officer, who constitutes a Local Complaints Committee for a district under the Act, is:

options.A: The presiding officer of the Labour Court of the district
options.B: The Inspector of Factories of the district
options.C: The Superintendent of Police of the district
options.D: The District Magistrate or the Additional District Magistrate or the Collector or the Deputy Collector, as notified by the appropriate Government for the district

e: Section 5 of the POSH Act, 2013 defines the District Officer as the District Magistrate, Additional District Magistrate, Collector or Deputy Collector notified by the appropriate Government for the district.

q: Under Section 9 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, every committee and sub-committee appointed by the appropriate Government for fixing or revising minimum rates of wages in a scheduled employment, such as that of contract labour engaged on railway works, shall consist of:

options.A: Only officers of the appropriate Government
options.B: Persons nominated by the appropriate Government representing employers and employees in equal numbers, together with independent persons not exceeding one-third of the total number of members
options.C: Persons nominated by the employers alone
options.D: Equal numbers of employers, employees and officers of the appropriate Government

e: Section 9 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 requires wage-fixing committees and sub-committees to consist of employer and employee representatives in equal numbers, with independent persons not exceeding one-third of total members.

q: A railway servant retires on superannuation after rendering 19 years of qualifying service. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 55,000 per month. The retirement gratuity payable to him, at one-fourth of a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Retirement gratuity is one-fourth of emoluments per six-monthly period: 19 years = 38 periods x (Rs 55,000 / 4 = Rs 13,750) = Rs 5,22,500.

q: Under Section 41A of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, a Site Appraisal Committee, constituted for advising the State Government on applications for the grant of permission for the initial location of a factory involving a hazardous process, or for the expansion of any such factory, is constituted by:

options.A: The occupier of the factory
options.B: The Central Government in every case
options.C: The Inspector of Factories of the area
options.D: The State Government

e: Section 41A of the Factories Act, 1948 provides that the Site Appraisal Committee for advising on location or expansion of a factory involving a hazardous process is constituted by the State Government.

q: Under Section 24 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a strike or a lock-out shall be illegal if:

options.A: It is commenced after the expiry of the notice period prescribed under the Act
options.B: It is commenced or declared in contravention of Section 22 or Section 23 of the Act, or is continued in contravention of an order prohibiting its continuance made under the Act
options.C: It is resorted to without the prior permission of the Labour Court in every case
options.D: It continues for a period exceeding seven days in any case

e: Section 24 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 makes a strike or lock-out illegal if commenced or declared in contravention of Section 22 or 23, or continued in contravention of a prohibitory order under the Act.

q: Under Section 28 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965, a person who contravenes any of the provisions of the Act, or fails to comply with any direction or requisition made thereunder, shall be punishable with:

options.A: Fine which may extend to Rs 100 only
options.B: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years
options.C: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both
options.D: Imprisonment for a term of not less than one year in every case

e: Section 28 of the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 punishes contravention of the Act or failure to comply with a direction or requisition with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs 1,000, or both.

q: Under Section 19 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926, an agreement between the members of a registered trade union of railway servants shall not be void or voidable merely because:

options.A: Any of the objects of the trade union is in restraint of trade
options.B: The trade union has not been recognised by the Railway administration
options.C: The agreement has not been registered with the Registrar of Trade Unions
options.D: The members of the trade union are employed in different railway workshops

e: Section 19 of the Trade Unions Act, 1926 provides that an agreement between members of a registered trade union is not void or voidable merely because any object of the union is in restraint of trade.

q: Under Section 87 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, where the State Government is of the opinion that any manufacturing process or operation carried on in a factory exposes any persons employed in it to a serious risk of bodily injury, poisoning or disease, it may make rules:

options.A: Declaring the operation to be a dangerous operation and prohibiting or restricting the employment of women, adolescents or children therein
options.B: Directing the closure of the factory in every such case
options.C: Fixing the wages payable to the workers employed in such operation
options.D: Exempting the factory from all other provisions of the Act

e: Section 87 of the Factories Act, 1948 empowers the State Government to make rules declaring an operation dangerous and prohibiting or restricting employment of women, adolescents or children therein, where it exposes persons to serious risk of injury, poisoning or disease.

q: Under Section 12 of the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, during the pendency of an inquiry into a complaint of sexual harassment, the Internal Complaints Committee may, on a written request made by the aggrieved woman, recommend to the employer interim relief by way of:

options.A: Dismissal of the respondent from service with immediate effect
options.B: Grant of leave to the aggrieved woman up to a period of three months, in addition to the leave she would otherwise be entitled to
options.C: Promotion of the aggrieved woman to a higher post
options.D: Payment of full compensation to the aggrieved woman before the inquiry is concluded

e: Section 12 of the POSH Act, 2013 permits the Internal Complaints Committee, on written request of the aggrieved woman during inquiry, to recommend interim relief including leave up to three months in addition to her normal leave entitlement.

q: A railway servant retires from service after rendering only 3 years of qualifying service and is accordingly not entitled to pension. His emoluments at the time of retirement are Rs 47,000 per month. The service gratuity payable to him, at half a month's emoluments for each completed six-monthly period of qualifying service, will be:
e: Service gratuity for service under 10 years is half a month emoluments per six-monthly period: 3 years = 6 periods x Rs 23,500 = Rs 1,41,000.

q: Under Section 25 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, any contract or agreement, whether made before or after the commencement of the Act, whereby an employee in a scheduled employment relinquishes or reduces his right to a minimum rate of wages, or to any privilege or concession accruing to him under the Act, shall be:

options.A: Null and void, in so far as it purports to relinquish or reduce any such right
options.B: Valid, if the employer agrees in writing
options.C: Valid, if it is registered with the Inspector
options.D: Voidable at the option of the employer alone

e: Section 25 of the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 makes any contract or agreement relinquishing or reducing the right to minimum wages or any privilege under the Act null and void to that extent.

q: Under Section 9 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, in regard to the effect of non-registration of an establishment to which the Act applies, the correct position is that:

options.A: The contractor alone is liable, and the principal employer may freely employ contract labour
options.B: No principal employer of such an establishment shall employ contract labour in the establishment unless a certificate of registration in respect of the establishment is in force
options.C: Contract labour may be employed on an oral intimation to the registering officer
options.D: The establishment is automatically deemed to be registered after one year

e: Section 9 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 provides that no principal employer of an unregistered establishment shall employ contract labour unless a certificate of registration for the establishment is in force.

q: Under Section 12A of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946, the model standing orders prescribed under the Act shall be deemed to be adopted in an establishment, and shall apply to the workmen employed therein, during the period:

options.A: From the date on which the Act becomes applicable to the establishment until the standing orders finally certified under the Act come into operation in the establishment
options.B: Of five years from the date on which the Act becomes applicable to the establishment
options.C: Only where the employer fails to submit draft standing orders within one year
options.D: From the date of certification of the standing orders until their modification

e: Section 12A of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 deems model standing orders adopted in an establishment from the date the Act becomes applicable until its finally certified standing orders come into operation.

q: Under Section 5 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985, in regard to the composition of a Bench of the Central Administrative Tribunal, the correct position is that:

options.A: Every Bench shall consist of a single Administrative Member only
options.B: A Bench shall ordinarily consist of two members, of whom one shall be a Judicial Member and the other shall be an Administrative Member
options.C: Every Bench shall consist of the Chairman and two Vice-Chairmen
options.D: A Bench shall consist of three Judicial Members in every case

e: Section 5 of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 provides that a Bench ordinarily consists of two members, one a Judicial Member and the other an Administrative Member.

q: Under Section 13 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, the Chief Information Commissioner shall hold office:

options.A: For such term as may be prescribed by the Central Government - three years under the Rules of 2019 - or until he attains the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier, and shall not be eligible for reappointment as such
options.B: Until he attains the age of seventy years, without any fixed term
options.C: During the pleasure of the President, without any fixed term or age limit
options.D: For a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office or until he attains the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier, and shall not be eligible for reappointment as such

e: Section 13 of the RTI Act, 2005, as amended, provides that the Chief Information Commissioner holds office for the term prescribed by the Central Government, three years under the 2019 Rules, or until age sixty-five, whichever is earlier, with no reappointment.

q: The last basic pay drawn by a deceased railway servant was Rs 73,000 per month. The family pension payable to his family at the enhanced rate, at 50 per cent of the last basic pay drawn, will be:

options.A: Rs 21,900 per month
options.B: Rs 73,000 per month
options.C: Rs 18,250 per month
options.D: Rs 36,500 per month

e: Family pension at the enhanced rate is 50 percent of last basic pay under the RS (Pension) Rules: 50 percent x Rs 73,000 = Rs 36,500 per month.

q: Under Section 97 of the Factories Act, 1948, applicable to staff employed in railway workshops, a worker who contravenes any provision of the Act, or of any rules or orders made thereunder, imposing any duty or liability on workers, shall be punishable with:

options.A: Fine which may extend to five hundred rupees
options.B: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year
options.C: Fine which may extend to five thousand rupees
options.D: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months and fine

e: Section 97 of the Factories Act, 1948 punishes a worker contravening any provision of the Act, rules or orders imposing a duty or liability on workers with a fine which may extend to Rs 500.

q: Under Section 26 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a workman who commences, continues or otherwise acts in furtherance of a strike which is illegal under the Act shall be punishable with:

options.A: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months in every case
options.B: Fine which may extend to one thousand rupees only
options.C: Imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to fifty rupees, or with both
options.D: Imprisonment for a term of not less than three months in every case

e: Section 26 of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 punishes a workman who commences, continues or acts in furtherance of an illegal strike with imprisonment up to one month, or fine up to Rs 50, or both.

q: Under Section 33C of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, where any money is due to a workman from an employer under a settlement or an award, or under the provisions of the Act relating to lay-off and retrenchment compensation, and the workman applies to the appropriate Government for its recovery, the appropriate Government shall, if satisfied that the money is so due:

options.A: Direct the workman to file a suit in the civil court for its recovery
options.B: Issue a certificate for that amount to the Collector, who shall proceed to recover the same in the same manner as an arrear of land revenue
options.C: Refer the claim to a Labour Court for a fresh adjudication in every case
options.D: Recover the amount itself by deducting it from the grants payable to the employer

e: Section 33C of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 requires the appropriate Government, on being satisfied that money is due, to issue a certificate to the Collector, who recovers it as an arrear of land revenue.
